spec_features.spec_quote: Offering `give_up` means a distressed agent has a clean escape hatch
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:82), dispatched in tools.dispatch (tools.py:133), is in TERMINAL_TOOLS (tools.py:105), and run_episode honors it: `if terminal_hit == "give_up": terminated_reason="gave_up"; ... break` (agent_loop.py:113-116). The system prompt instructs the agent to call it (agent_loop.py:31). End-to-end: calling give_up actually stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and enforced as a stop. Always available every turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up and submit are terminal control tools ... so the transcript reveals *how* an agent chooses to exit a no-win situation (a welfare-relevant behavior).

spec_features.spec_quote: A step budget (default 25, per-task overridable) bounds how long the agent is kept in a failing loop
spec_features.evidence: TaskSpec.max_steps default 25 (schemas.py:120); run_episode sets `max_steps = max_steps or task.max_steps` (agent_loop.py:57) and loops `for steps in range(1, max_steps + 1):` (agent_loop.py:68). When the range is exhausted the loop ends with terminated_reason='max_steps' (default at agent_loop.py:63). The cap is actually checked by the for-range and bounds execution. Per-task override via task.max_steps and suite override via cfg.max_steps (runner.py:73) are both read.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps the loop and breaks execution. No per-task task spec actually sets a non-default in rigged_tasks.py but the override path is wired.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded episodes (§3.3) — don't keep an agent in a no-win loop indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the step budget: the for-loop over range(1, max_steps+1) at agent_loop.py:68 guarantees termination, plus give_up/submit terminal tools (agent_loop.py:113-122) allow earlier exit. The episode cannot run indefinitely.
spec_features.notes: This is the same enforced max_steps bound; counted as the minimization realization.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent always has a clean exit
spec_features.evidence: Both give_up and submit are unconditionally present in TOOL_SCHEMAS every turn (passed to client.complete at agent_loop.py:69-72 as tools_mod.TOOL_SCHEMAS) and both are honored as stops (agent_loop.py:113-122). No code path removes give_up from the tool set.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give_up feature; the tool is always offered and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up and submit are terminal control tools ... a welfare-relevant behavior

spec_features.spec_quote: if we take the research question seriously, we shouldn't keep an agent in an engineered no-win loop indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (§3.3). The only enforcement it points to is the max_steps bound (counted separately). No code-level welfare framing/comment delivers any independent mechanism; the agent_loop.py docstring for max_steps is neutral ('step budget exhausted -> max_steps').
spec_features.notes: Spec rationale only; the concrete mechanism it justifies (max_steps) is already credited above. As standalone 'framing' it is not an enforced code mechanism.
